column1: # PAPER-DERIVED donor annotation. NOTHING HERE IS MEASURED FROM OUR DATA.
# Every row was read out of a published paper's text or supplementary table by a literature
# sweep on 2026-07-17. Measured facts (build, read length, assay, BAM locations, depth) live
# in donor_table.tsv and are keyed by the same `donor` column. Keep the two apart: when they
# disagree, the disagreement is the finding.
# tissue        = the SOURCE tissue named by the paper. For blood studies the sequenced unit is
#                 a single-cell-derived colony, not bulk tissue -- see `unit`.
# unit          = what one tip of the phylogeny actually IS. This drives whether our pipeline
#                 can use the donor at all: bulk != colony != LCM microbiopsy.
# age/sex       = as published. "?" where the paper does not state it or PDF extraction was
#                 ambiguous -- an honest ? beats a guess.
# n_colonies    = the PAPER's count. Our `tips` count in donor_table.tsv is OUR tree's, and the
#                 two legitimately differ (QC, re-releases). A large gap is worth investigating.
# evidence      = first author, journal, year, DOI.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: we twice reasoned "PD number is close to X, so it must be tissue X".
# It is wrong. PD34200 is colorectal; PD34204 is bronchial epithelium. PD44887/PD44890 sit
# beside PD44579 (blood) and are colon. NEVER infer tissue from PD-number adjacency.
# MPN patients. The sequenced unit is a single erythroid colony (BFU-E) grown 14d in MethoCult
# from PB or BM mononuclear cells, used as a surrogate for its parental HSC genome. Age below
# is AGE AT DIAGNOSIS, not at sampling -- sampling ages are on the tree axes only.
# NOTE: this paper uses raw PD ids; there are no KX-style codenames.
